A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same EM-LLM work. Their complete text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original LongBench evaluations, PG-19 segmentation comparisons, analyses against human event boundaries and component ablations.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical results and adds evaluations across models and benchmarks, RAG/full-context comparisons, retrieval diagnostics and runtime measurements.

M1.justification: The surprise-based segmentation, boundary refinement and two-buffer retrieval algorithm remain. Appendix C.2 introduces execution adaptations for very long sequences: disk-backed LRU memory management, optional CPU offloading of representative tokens and layer parallelisation across GPUs.

E1.justification: V2 retains LongBench, PG-19 and the human podcasts, while adding six ∞-Bench tasks covering code debugging, mathematical finding, long-book multiple-choice questions and KV/passkey/number retrieval. Figure 1 also adds an extended passkey-retrieval scenario reaching 10 million tokens.

E2.justification: V1's downstream comparison uses InfLLM. V2 retains it and adds RAG pipelines using all-mpnet-base-v2 and NV-Embed-v2 in Table 8, plus full-context inference alongside NV-Embed-v2 RAG in Table 9. These introduce substantially different comparator families.

E3.justification: Alongside the retained 4K+2K evaluation, v2 adds LLaMA-3/3.1 configurations with 4K+4K contexts and Phi-3/3.5 configurations with 1K+3K contexts. New experiments introduce a 300-word, top-five-chunk RAG protocol and timing measurements over 100 chunks of 512 tokens. These do not establish that the original experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V2 extends component ablations across additional models and ∞-Bench, adds a layer-specific retrieval case study in Figure 5, and extends human-segmentation comparisons to Mistral and LLaMA-3 in Figures 7–8. Runtime profiling and Figure 9's configuration comparisons add further analyses. V1's sensitivity plots remain as Figures 10–11.

E5.justification: V2 Figure 5 adds box-and-whisker summaries of retrieval-ratio variability across more than 500 chunks. Existing PG-19 plus/minus statistics and human-data plot bands are retained. Neither version reports a repeated-seed protocol or confidence intervals for downstream benchmark performance.

E6.justification: V2 adds extensive benchmark, comparator, model and efficiency results. Corresponding original LongBench entries also change: the S variant's PassageRetrieval score changes from 85.42 in v1 Table 1 to 82.67 in v2 Table 3, while InfLLM remains 64.00. The configuration selection behind these revisions is unexplained. PG-19 Table 2 values remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 3.4 revises the stated total retrieved-event count from k = ks + kc + 2 to k = ks + kc. The graph-based definitions, complexity argument and two k-NN/softmax approximation lemmas otherwise remain unchanged; the original complexity analysis and proof move to Appendices C.1 and E.1.

C1.justification: V1 foregrounds a 4.3% LongBench improvement over InfLLM and human-like event segmentation. V2 broadens the main claims to performance across five base LLMs and two benchmarks, superiority over RAG and full-context inference, and successful retrieval across 10 million tokens. The underlying human-memory contribution remains.

C2.justification: V2 adds substantive explanations attributing advantages over RAG to layer-specific retrieval and advantages over full-context inference to reduced attention dilution. Appendix A.2 discusses retriever-capacity bottlenecks and pipeline complexity, while Appendix C.2 explains growing memory and retrieval-time costs and offloading tradeoffs. Existing cognitive interpretations and contiguity qualifications largely remain.

D1.justification: V2 supplies explicit backbone identifiers, RAG construction settings, Hugging Face integration details and offloading/parallelisation procedures. Appendix C.2 newly documents four-GPU nodes with 32GB per GPU, CPU-memory requirements, timing methodology and API use for full-context results. V1 provides substantially less implementation and hardware information.

R1.justification: The existing long-context and episodic-memory reviews, including novelty relative to InfLLM, largely remain. V2 adds focused positioning against RAG and references covering NV-Embed, all-mpnet-base-v2, MTEB, RAG enhancements and ∞-Bench. Publication-status updates to existing citations do not introduce new works.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and much of the method and related-work prose remain. V2 revises the abstract and experimental framing, condenses the discussion and conclusion, and reorganises the supplemental material into thematic appendices with a contents list. These are focused editorial and organisational revisions.

P2.justification: V2 redesigns the main performance table around task groups and multiple models, and adds comparison, diagnostic, ablation and resource displays. It introduces the opening radar/scalability figure and redraws a subset of the human results for the main text. Original figures are preserved elsewhere, including v1 Figures 3–5 as v2 Figures 6, 10–11.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially addresses v1's narrow downstream validation and largely theoretical efficiency discussion through broader model and benchmark testing, RAG/full-context comparisons, extreme-length retrieval evidence and concrete resource measurements. Implementation details also improve reproducibility. Reporting inconsistencies qualify this gain: Section 4.1's 30.5%/11.5% RAG improvements do not reconcile with Table 9, and Table 4's LLaMA-3 ∞-Bench results contradict uniformly superior performance. These issues limit claim reliability but do not outweigh the substantial improvement in evidence and transparency.
